answers.d01: 似然回答：固定已经看到的数据，哪个假设能更好地解释它？抛硬币10次得7次正面。若正面概率p=0.5，出现这批结果的概率约0.117；若p=0.7，约0.267。这0.267就是p=0.7时数据的似然——数据固定、参数在变，比较的是「哪个参数让这批数据更不意外」。注意它不是p本身的概率，似然只用来横向比较参数。后验回答另一方向的问题：看完数据后，p取各种值的概率分布是多少？贝叶斯公式给出：后验 ∝ 先验 × 似然。似然是数据对参数的支持度，是桥梁；先验是看数据之前的判断；两者相乘归一得到后验。若先验均匀，后验形状完全由似然决定；先验偏一边，结论就被拉过去。分清方向：似然是给定参数问数据，后验是给定数据问参数。
answers.d02: Averages hide spread. Two classes both average 70; in one everyone scores 68–72, in the other scores run 40–100. You need a second number for scatter. Population variance is the average squared distance from the mean: σ² = (1/N)·Σ(xᵢ−μ)². Take {2, 4, 6}: mean is 4, deviations are −2, 0, +2. They sum to zero—ups and downs cancel, which is why we can't just average them. Squaring makes every deviation positive and punishes big misses harder: a point 10 away counts as 100. Here variance is (4+0+4)/3 ≈ 2.67. Its units are squared, so we usually take the square root—the standard deviation, back in original units. Change one value from 6 to 60 and the variance explodes, showing its sensitivity to outliers. (For samples meant to estimate a larger population, divide by n−1; the reason comes later.)
answers.d04: You have one free afternoon: nap, gym, study, or a freelance gig paying $80. Opportunity cost is the value of the single best option you give up. Choose the gym and your cost isn't nap + study + $80—it's only the highest-valued alternative: $80, or the lost rest, if you value the nap most. That's the measure: what you would actually have picked instead, not everything else combined. The unit needn't be money; 'value' means what the option was worth to you. This reframes 'free': a free concert costs the afternoon you spent on it. Watch how the judgment shifts: if the gig is cancelled, the gym suddenly costs only a nap. The habit it builds is asking 'compared to what?'—a choice is good or bad only relative to the best alternative, and that comparison is the real reasoning tool.
answers.d05: 检测阳性，你得病的概率是99%吗？不是——它还取决于有多少人本来就患病。设10000人体检，患病率1%：约100人患病，99%被查出，约99人阳性；其余9900名健康人误报率1%，也约99人阳性。阳性共198人，真患病的只有99人：P(病|阳性)≈99/198=50%。贝叶斯公式就是这步的压缩：P(病|阳)=P(阳|病)×P(病)÷P(阳)。关键分清方向：P(阳|病)是灵敏度——给定病人，检测呈阳性的概率；P(病|阳)才是你关心的——拿到阳性后患病的概率。两者方向相反，被基础患病率拉开：病越罕见，阳性里误报占比越大。条件变化：若筛查对象是高危人群，患病率10%，同一种检测下P(病|阳)≈0.099/0.108≈92%。同一试剂，换个基础率，结论截然不同——所以筛查阳性后需要复查。
answers.d06: A cache is a fast copy of slow data: instead of hitting the database on every page view, you store the rendered product page and reuse it. Invalidation is the rule for when that copy must be thrown away or refreshed because the original changed. Say the cache holds a price for 60 seconds; the seller cuts the price, and for up to a minute customers see the old one. That's the core trade-off: copies are fast but can go stale. Common strategies: expire after a TTL (simple, but stale for a bounded window); delete the cached key whenever the database row updates, so the next read refetches; or update the cache on every write. It's hard because one fact lives in many cached places across machines, and you must find all of them. If data never changes, no problem; if it must always be fresh, either don't cache or pay the synchronous cost.
answers.d07: 某海滨城市统计发现：冰淇淋销量越高，溺水人数越多，两者高度相关。能下结论「吃冰淇淋导致溺水」吗？不能。相关只说明两个量同涨同跌；因果要求「改变A，B随之改变」。这里有个共同原因：夏天气温高，既让人多买冰淇淋，也让更多人下水，溺水随之增多——这叫混杂变量。区分方法一：控制共同原因——只在夏天内部或按月份分层比较，冰淇淋与溺水的关联基本消失，因果链断裂。方法二：随机实验——随机分组让人吃或不吃冰淇淋，溺水率不会因此不同，因为随机切断了与气温的关联。条件变化：若相关背后有真实机制（如某药确实降血压），控制住混杂后相关依然存在，干预也能改变结果。还要警惕反向因果：可能是B导致A。相关是发现因果的线索，裁决要靠控制变量或实验。
answers.d08: Compound growth means growth is proportional to what you already have: interest earns its own interest. At 10% a year, $1,000 becomes $1,100, then $1,210, then $1,331—the increases grow because each is computed on a bigger base. After n years the amount is P(1+r)ⁿ, not P×(1+r×n). The starting amount P matters because it is the base being multiplied: starting with $2,000 at the same rate gives exactly double at every point. Time interacts with it sharply: $1,000 at 10% grows to about $17,450 in 30 years but about $45,250 in 40—the last ten years add more than the first thirty, which is why starting early beats starting big. The same math works against you: debt and inflation compound too. It requires a steady rate and reinvestment—spend the interest each year and growth stays linear.
answers.v01: 打个比方：一个学生把每道练习题的答案背得滚瓜烂熟，模拟卷次次满分，一到新题就崩。这就是过拟合——模型把训练数据里的细节和噪声也「背」了下来，而不是学到真正的规律。怎么辨认：在见过的数据上表现很好，在没见过的数据上明显变差，这个落差就是标志；反过来，两边都差是欠拟合——连规律都没学到。为什么发生：模型太灵活或数据太少，自由度大到足以把噪声也精确拟合进去。数据里既有规律也有随机噪声，模型分不清两者。怎么办：增加数据、换更简单的模型、留出一部分数据专做检验——只有检验集上表现也好，才说明学到了规律。条件变化：数据多了，噪声被平均掉，死记硬背不再占便宜。迁移到人：只见过典型病例的医生，遇到非典型症状就容易误诊——样本太窄，规律学偏了。
answers.v02: Search your library for 'jaguar': 10 results come back, 8 match what you wanted, and the library holds 20 matching documents total. Precision asks: of what was returned, how much was right? 8/10 = 80%. It measures junk—low precision means wading through irrelevant hits. Recall asks: of everything that exists, how much was found? 8/20 = 40%. It measures misses. The two pull against each other: return only the single most confident hit and precision is 100% while recall is 5%; return the whole catalog and recall hits 100% with tiny precision. Which matters depends on the task: legal discovery needs high recall; a search box showing one answer needs high precision. Both require knowing the full set of true matches, which is why they're evaluation metrics, not live signals.
answers.v03: 自然选择不是动物主动努力变强，而是「变异先发生，环境来筛选」。长颈鹿不是伸脖子够高叶把脖子拉长的；真实过程是：后代中本来就随机存在脖子长短不一的变异（来自基因突变和重组），脖子稍长的个体吃到更多树叶，饿死得少、留下更多后代，「长脖子」基因在下一代中的比例升高。如此一代代下去，种群的平均脖子长度提高。关键三点：变异随机产生，不是练出来的；选择作用于已有变异，不定向制造变异；改变的是种群的基因频率，不是某只个体在一生中的变化。成立条件：变异可遗传、变异影响生存繁殖、资源有限产生竞争。再看细菌抗药性：不是细菌「努力学会」抗药，而是药物把不抗药的杀死，幸存的抗药者大量繁殖，种群被筛选成抗药的。口诀：先有随机差异，后有环境淘汰。
answers.v04: An idempotent operation produces the same effect whether it runs once or many times: applying it again changes nothing. It matters in distributed systems because networks retry. Your payment POST times out—did the server process it? Unknown. The client retries; without idempotency you're charged twice. The standard fix: the client attaches an idempotency key (a unique token); the server records each processed key with its result and, on a repeat, returns the stored response instead of executing again. Some operations are naturally idempotent: GET (read only), PUT (set value to X—doing it twice still leaves X), DELETE. POST 'create order' is not. Design costs: the server needs storage for keys and a retention policy. One boundary: idempotency covers retries of the same request—if the underlying data changed between calls, a repeat can legitimately return a different answer.
answers.v05: 熵度量一个随机结果平均有多难猜，也就是看到结果时平均获得多少信息。公式 H = −Σ pᵢ log pᵢ：每种结果的意外程度（−log p，概率越小越意外）按其概率加权平均。为什么均匀分布最不确定：所有选项同样可能时，你没有任何理由偏爱某一个，猜中的把握最小。两面各半的硬币熵是1比特；90%正面的硬币熵约0.47比特——你几乎总猜正面，很少猜错，不确定自然小。偏向的分布把概率压在少数结果上，可猜的空间被压缩；均匀分布把概率摊平，每个结果都同样可能出乎意料。条件要清楚：「均匀最大」是在结果个数固定的前提下成立，选项集合变了要重算。熵描述的是整个概率分布的形态，不是某一次的结果；单位（比特等）由对数的底决定。
answers.v06: Two processes each hold one resource and each wants the other's: Process 1 holds lock A and requests B; Process 2 holds B and requests A. Each waits for the other to release, and neither ever will—it's waiting, not working. That's deadlock. It needs four conditions at once: resources are exclusive; holders keep them while requesting more; nothing can forcibly take a resource away; and the waits form a circle. Break any one and deadlock disappears. Reorder requests so everyone acquires locks in the same order (A then B)—now P2 waits for A before ever taking B, and the circle can't form. Other fixes: timeouts, or requesting everything up front. Condition change: if P1 had asked for B before taking A, both would simply queue and proceed. Real databases detect the circle and roll back one transaction; the same shape appears in traffic gridlock and threads contending for file locks.
answers.v07: 公共物品同时满足两个条件：非排他——挡不住不付钱的人使用；非竞争——多一人使用不减少他人的使用。路灯是典型：照你也照邻居，无法把谁排除在外。问题由此产生：既然不付钱也能用，理性的选择就是不付钱，等别人出钱自己白享——这就是搭便车。例：小区十户想装路灯，成本1000元，每户受益折合500元。每户都想等别家出钱，结果谁都不出，路灯装不成，十户各损失500元。注意这不是人品问题，而是激励结构造成的集体困境：对个体理性的选择，汇总成对集体的坏结果。正因为收不到钱，公共物品通常供给不足，需要税收、物业费这类强制分摊来筹资。对照私人物品如面包：可排他、可竞争，不付钱拿不到，市场就能有效供给。判断就看那两个条件。
answers.v08: Little's law: L = λW. The average number of items in a system equals the arrival rate times the average time each item spends inside. Coffee shop: 10 customers arrive per minute and each spends 3 minutes ordering and waiting, so on average 30 people are inside. Units check: customers/minute × minutes = customers. Why it holds: at steady state everyone who enters eventually leaves, so average inventory must equal flow rate × residence time. The payoff: measure any two, compute the third. A server receiving 100 requests/second, each taking 0.2 seconds, must have about 20 requests in flight—if it can hold only 10, latency must drop or the queue grows. Conditions: steady state (rates roughly stable, nothing overflowing) and all three measured over the same system boundary. Count 'in line' but time 'including service' and the numbers won't match.
